# Delicat Builder V9 — audit, final section

**Tree audited:** `/home/user/snowy-boat-a2d8/plugin/delicat-builder-v9` at commit `723148d`, `Version: 9.2.0-pro.40` (`delicat-builder-v9.php:6`), working tree clean. The brief said pro.38; it is not. Three of the six findings handed to me were written against pro.38/pro.39 code and **are already fixed in the tree** — I dropped them (details in §1b). Three survive, and I re-reproduced all three against the current files.

**The surviving set is small: three findings, one of which is the only one that costs money.** I did not pad it.

---

## 1. Surviving findings, by real impact

### F1 — A declined card permanently locks a signed-in customer out of checkout
`includes/class-delicat-builder-express-payment.php:222` (retention), `:152` (reclaim refusal), `:168` + `:264` (scope)

`guard_classic()` is hooked on `woocommerce_checkout_process` priority 1 (`:264`) and takes a per-customer mutex for **every signed-in classic checkout, on every gateway** — the comment at `:170` says so explicitly. WooCommerce creates the order *before* charging, so `record['creating']` and `record['order_id']` are already set when the gateway is asked to charge. If the charge fails — declined card, gateway timeout, exception in `process_payment` — `woocommerce_payment_successful_result` never fires with `success`, so `context['finished']` is never set. `shutdown()` at `:222` then releases the guard only when *both* `creating` and `order_id` are empty, so it is retained. On the next attempt `begin()` cannot insert, and `reclaim_abandoned()` refuses at `:152` on `! empty($record['creating'])` **regardless of age** — the 300 s `ABANDONED_AFTER` check at `:153` is never reached. The customer sees *"Un paiement est déjà en cours ou à vérifier dans vos commandes."* forever. Nothing was charged. Only an admin clicking "Libérer après vérification" frees them.

**Proof (re-run against this tree, PHP 8.4):** `/tmp/dbaudit/test-express-lock.php` and `test-express-lock2.php` require the real class and drive the real WooCommerce callback order against a fake `$wpdb` implementing the exact semantics of the four SQL shapes the class uses.

```
ATTEMPT 1  gateway DECLINES
  after shutdown: delicat_payment_active_42 = a2e6e085-…
  record = {"status":"pending","order_id":1001,"hash":"CARTHASH1","creating":true}
ATTEMPT 2  same customer, valid card, 10 min later   -> BLOCKED
ATTEMPT 3  24 h later, brand-new cart                -> BLOCKED
Variant B  gateway returns result=failure            -> BLOCKED, reclaim_abandoned()=false after 24 h
Control    successful checkout                       -> guard released
```

**Fix.** Two changes, either alone reduces this to an edge case; do both:
1. Scope `guard_classic()` to the wallet/express gateway it was designed for instead of every signed-in classic checkout (`:168`). The double-charge risk it guards is wallet-specific.
2. Make `reclaim_abandoned()` able to reclaim on `creating`/`order_id` when the order is demonstrably unpaid: after the `ABANDONED_AFTER` age check, `$o = wc_get_order($record['order_id']); if ($o && ! $o->is_paid() && $o->needs_payment()) return self::release(...)`. Keep the current refusal only while the order is paid or its state is unknown.

**Confidence: high.** Mechanism proven end-to-end in a harness; the only thing I could not exercise is a real WooCommerce gateway.

---

### F2 — The cache-protection gate and the cache-render gate disagree: six request shapes print the shopper's real basket **and** ship with no cache headers at all
`includes/class-delicat-builder-security.php:588`

Two gates must agree and do not.

- **Render gate.** `shared_document()` (`:435`) returns `public_cache_allowed()` (`:313`). When false, the header cart panel prints the visitor's real basket — product names, thumbnails, quantities, line prices, subtotal (`includes/class-delicat-builder-header-runtime.php:272-310`, auto-rendered on `wp_body_open` for every front-end route, `:26`/`:212`).
- **Protection gate.** `protect_private_response()` (`:597`, hooked `template_redirect` priority 0 at `:61`) asks `response_cache_tier()`. On `'shared'` it returns at `:599` — no `DONOTCACHEPAGE`, no `nocache_headers()`, no `Cache-Control`, no `Vary`. WordPress adds none either.

Line 588 decides `'shared'` from only `is_user_logged_in() || has_private_cookie()`. `public_cache_allowed()` additionally requires `query_is_cache_safe()` (the pro.30 allowlist, `:374`) and `Multi_Currency::public_cache_variant_required()`. Fail *only* one of those two and the plugin both personalises the document and declines to protect it. This is a pro.30 leftover: before pro.30 the Woo cart cookies were in `has_private_cookie()` and covered these cases; pro.30 removed them and widened `public_cache_allowed()` without widening the tier predicate.

**Proof (re-run against this tree):** `…/scratchpad/test-tier-vs-shared.php` loads the real `class-delicat-builder-security.php`, guest, GET, Woo cart cookies present:

```
/ (clean guest with cart)            shared  pub=true  shared_doc=true   ok
/?paged=2                           shared  true      true              ok
/?fbclid=x                          shared  true      true              ok
/?s=rum  (site search)              shared  false     false   *** UNPROTECTED + PERSONALISED ***
/?p=123                             shared  false     false   ***
/boutique/?mtm_source=ig            shared  false     false   ***
/boutique/?really_anything=1        shared  false     false   ***
/produit/rum/?attribute_pa_size=m   shared  false     false   ***
/?lang=en                           shared  false     false   ***
/panier/                            sensitive …                        ok
/?add-to-cart=55                    sensitive …                        ok
/ with dmc_currency=USD             personal  …                        ok
/ logged in                         personal  …                        ok
DIVERGENT SCENARIOS: 6
```

Note `/?s=rum` — plain site search with a cart — is the everyday case. None of the four `prepare_cache_policy()` handlers fire on a search results page, so line 588 is the only gate there.

**Fix (one line, verified to cost no cacheable traffic):**

```php
if ( is_user_logged_in() || self::has_private_cookie() || ! self::public_cache_allowed() ) {
    return 'personal';
}
return 'shared';
```

`…/scratchpad/test-fix.php` re-runs the table with this applied: all six divergent rows become `personal`, and the three rows pro.30 was built to win back (clean guest with cart, `?paged=2`, `?fbclid=`) stay `shared`. Add a regression test asserting `('shared' === response_cache_tier()) === shared_document()` over the `tests/test-cache-gate.php` scenario table.

**Confidence: high on the divergence** (proven, and the render side is confirmed by reading `cart_panel_markup()`). **Medium on the cross-user leak actually firing in production** — it requires a shared cache in front that stores HTML without a `Cache-Control` directive. LiteSpeed page cache will; Cloudflare does not cache HTML by default unless a Cache-Everything rule is on, and I could not inspect this store's CF config. Treat it as "the plugin has stopped defending itself", not "a leak is confirmed happening".

---

### F3 — `?dbp_state=1` answers on `init:5` and walks straight through maintenance mode's API lock
`pro/class-dbp-state.php:42` (hook), `:64` (`maybe_respond`)

With the store closed and *"Fermer aussi les API"* on (`lock_api=1`, the default), Maintenance registers exactly three gates (`includes/class-delicat-builder-maintenance.php:51-60`): `guard_early` on `init:1`, which returns early unless `wp_doing_ajax()` or `XMLRPC_REQUEST`; `guard_rest`; and `guard_frontend` on `template_redirect:0`. `GET /?dbp_state=1` is neither ajax nor XML-RPC, so `guard_early` falls through, `maybe_respond` answers at `init:5` and `exit`s — `template_redirect` never runs. I confirmed by grep that `pro/class-dbp-state.php` contains no maintenance check of any kind.

**Proof (re-run against this tree):** `…/scratchpad/test-maintenance-dbp-state.php` loads the real Maintenance and DBP_State classes and fires a priority-ordered `init` then `template_redirect`:

```
scenario dbp_state (store CLOSED, lock_api=1, signed-in customer)
  [hook] init(1) -> Maintenance::guard_early
  [hook] init(5) -> DBP_State::maybe_respond
{"ok":true,"user":{"id":42,"loggedIn":true,"name":"Jean Baptiste"},
 "cart":{"count":3,"subtotal":"HTG 4,500.00"},"wallet":{"balance":"HTG 1,250.75","raw":1250.75},
 "nonces":{"state":"…","wc":"…","addToCart":"…","rest":"NONCE(wp_rest)"}}
```

The sibling endpoint `?wc-ajax=delicat_session` **is** correctly 503'd by `guard_frontend` in the same run, which shows the intended behaviour.

**Fix.** Gate it at the endpoint, since it short-circuits before everything else. At the top of `maybe_respond()`, after the `Sec-Fetch-Site` check: if `Delicat_Builder_V9_Maintenance` exists, is locked, and `lock_api` is set, `status_header(503)` and send `{ok:false,error:'maintenance'}`. Expose a small public `Maintenance::api_locked()` rather than widening `settings()`. Belt-and-braces: extend `guard_early()` (`:336`) so that with `lock_api` on it also 503s any non-admin front-end request carrying a Builder API flag (`dbp_state`, `dbp_nav`, `dbp_fragment`, `delicat_product_fragment`, `dbv9_fragment`), not just `wp_doing_ajax()`/XML-RPC.

**Confidence: high on the bypass, low on severity.** No privilege escalation — it serves the *caller's own* session and nonces. The real cost is that a shutdown the owner relies on during an incident does not actually stop scripted reads or nonce minting. All three verification lenses rated it low; I keep it because it is cheap to fix and it makes a documented promise false.

---

### 1b. Findings I dropped after re-verification

| Claimed | Why dropped |
|---|---|
| `server-engine.php:424` — `! empty($_GET)` makes every ad-tagged landing private and defines `DONOTCACHEPAGE` | **Fixed in this tree.** The gate is now `server-engine.php:453`: `$private = is_user_logged_in() \|\| self::sensitive_request() \|\| ! self::query_is_cache_safe() \|\| self::has_private_cookie();`, with the helper at `:302-307` delegating to the pro.30 allowlist. Line 424 is blank. The only surviving `! empty($_GET)` text is the PRO40 docblock describing the fix. |
| `assets.php:332` — post-update the homepage ships `all-components.min.css` (176 KB) until someone opens a Builder admin screen | **Largely fixed.** `class-delicat-builder-compiler.php` is now loaded on **every** non-Builder admin request (`delicat-builder-v9.php:1057`, inside the `is_admin() && ! wp_doing_ajax()` else-branch at `:1017`), so the first visit to any wp-admin page repairs the manifest. A residual window remains (see §2, item 2) but the "indefinitely" claim is no longer true. |
| `dbp-nav.js:362` — `history.scrollRestoration='manual'` is never reset, so Back from a product page dumps the shopper at the top | **Fixed in this tree.** `hardNavigate()` now resets it: `pro/assets/dbp-nav.js:584`, `try { if (history.scrollRestoration) history.scrollRestoration = 'auto'; }`, with a PRO40 comment at `:570-583` describing exactly this scenario. `applySwap` still sets `'manual'` at `:393`, which is correct while the engine owns the document. |

The three fixed items were all real at the version the brief named. Do not re-open them.

---

## 2. What would still make delicastoreha.com slow after pro.37–pro.40 are installed

Ordered by expected win. **None of this is measured on the live site** — see §3.

1. **Every product pageview fires a second full WordPress + WooCommerce bootstrap.** `pro/class-dbp-state.php:289` sets `initial => 1` whenever the route is `product` (or cart/checkout/account/wallet) — **even for a guest with no cookies and no cart**. `pro/assets/dbp-state.js:205-207` then fetches `/?dbp_state=1` with `cache:'no-store'` on `load`. On the most-visited route that is roughly 2× the origin PHP request count. It is idle-scheduled so it does not hurt LCP on a fast connection, but on a saturated shared host it lengthens TTFB for *every* visitor, including the cached ones. **Win:** drop `'product'` from the `initial` route list and let the endpoint fire only when a cart/session/currency cookie is present or on the first interaction. Cheapest large win in the codebase.
2. **The post-update CSS window.** After an auto-update, until the merchant next opens *any* wp-admin page, managed pages serve `storefront-chrome.min.css` (95,704 B) **plus** `all-components.min.css` (180,614 B) = 276 KB of render-blocking CSS instead of ~95 KB + a ~40 KB per-page bundle. On an auto-updating store with an absent owner that window can be days. **Win:** move `Compiler::maybe_recompile_for_version()` onto the `upgrader_process_complete` / `plugins_loaded` version-drift path that already exists for `DBP_Kernel::deploy_check`, so the repair happens at update time and not on an admin visit. Alternatively drop the plain version-equality test from the manifest validity check — `layout_hash` + `source_signature` already prove the bundle matches the sources.
3. **The plugin forbids LiteSpeed from optimising any of its own assets.** `delicat-builder-v9.php:1260-1266` adds `delicat-builder-v9/assets/` and `delicat-builder-v9/pro/assets/` to `litespeed_optimize_css_excludes`, `litespeed_optimize_js_excludes`, `litespeed_optm_js_defer_exc`, `litespeed_optm_gm_js_exc` **and** `litespeed_optm_css_async_exc`. So none of it can be combined, deferred or async-loaded. Each stylesheet is a separate render-blocking request forever. That is a deliberate correctness trade (it is what makes the blocking sheet safe), but it means the storefront's critical path is fully hand-managed and LiteSpeed cannot help. **Win:** narrow the exclusion to the sheets that genuinely must block (`storefront-chrome`, the compiled per-page bundle) and let LiteSpeed combine the rest. Medium effort, medium risk — test on staging.
4. **The critical-CSS subsystem is currently inert, and costs HTML bytes.** `component:base` minifies to 28,704 B against a hard 20,000-byte inline budget, so it is dropped on all 14 section types; and since nothing is deferred (item 3), the inline block is purely additive — 5.3–8.9 KB of inline CSS per response duplicating bytes the blocking sheet delivers anyway. **Win:** small but free. Either raise the budget and actually defer something, or switch the subsystem off and reclaim the inline bytes. (Carried over from a refuted finding; I did not re-run that harness, so treat the byte figures as the previous lens's measurement.)
5. **Cache misses from query keys outside the pro.30 allowlist.** `query_is_cache_safe()` (`security.php:374`) allows `utm_*`, `filter_*`, `query_type_*`, `fbclid`, `gclid`, `paged`, `orderby` and friends; **anything else bypasses both the page cache and the fragment cache**. Real traffic that still misses: site search `?s=`, translation plugins `?lang=`, Matomo `?mtm_*`, WooCommerce variation deep links `?attribute_pa_*`. The plugin already ships the escape hatch — `apply_filters('delicat_builder_v9_cache_safe_query_keys', ...)` at `security.php:394`. **Win:** audit one week of the store's real URLs and add its own content-neutral keys through that filter. Note this interacts with F2: fix F2 *first*, or widening the allowlist widens the set of pages that ship personalised-and-unprotected.
6. **No persistent object cache.** `includes/class-delicat-builder-query-cache.php:19` records that Hostinger's default has none, so every query-cache and server-fragment entry lands in `wp_options` as a transient (`:114`, `:127`), and expired entries are swept on only ~5% of admin requests (`:33`). **Win:** install Redis/Memcached with a drop-in. The class is already `wp_cache_*`-aware and will use it automatically. This is a hosting change, not a code change, and it is the single highest-leverage infrastructure move.
7. **Not a win — checked and dismissed.** I tested whether the large unminified stylesheets (`purchase-native.css` 70 KB, `calc.css` 55 KB, `theme-system.css` 44 KB, `dsb-modern-menu.css` 42 KB) would benefit from minification. Stripping comments and whitespace saves 0–2% on all of them (only `components/products.css` gives 14%). They are effectively already minimal. Do not spend time there.

---

## 3. Not covered / could not verify

- **The live site was never measured.** The brief and the owner both asked for a speed test of delicastoreha.com. The agent proxy refuses the CONNECT tunnel: `curl: (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`, `code=000` in 0.24 s. So **every performance statement above is derived from code, not from a measurement**, and the ordering is an estimate. To close this, run from a machine with network access: `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{time_starttransfer} %{time_total} %{size_download}\n' 'https://delicastoreha.com/'` and the same for `/?fbclid=test`, a product URL, and `/?s=rum`; a mismatch in TTFB between the clean and `?fbclid=` homepage would confirm or refute item 5, and `curl -I` on each would show whether `x-litespeed-cache: hit` is ever produced. A PageSpeed/WebPageTest run on the homepage and one product page would settle items 1–4 in minutes.
- **No live WordPress install.** Everything here is harness work: the real classes loaded under stubbed WordPress functions on PHP 8.4 CLI. That verifies logic and control flow, not plugin interactions, theme behaviour, the actual LiteSpeed configuration, or the Cloudflare cache rules in front of this store — which is precisely the gap in F2's severity.
- **Not examined in this pass:** the admin/editor surface (~beyond load gating), the PWA and service-worker layer, the reviews, notifications and live-selling modules, the identity bridge, image/media handling and thumbnail generation, database schema and index health, and anything about the theme or other active plugins.
- **F1's gateway path** was exercised through a fake `$wpdb` and hand-driven WooCommerce callbacks, not a real WooCommerce. The callback ordering I asserted (order created before charge) is WooCommerce's documented behaviour, not something I ran.
- Findings already fixed in pro.37–pro.40 were not re-derived; I only checked that the fixes are present, which is how §1b's three drops were established.
